name: DAVERAGE
description: DAVERAGE returns the arithmetic mean of the numeric values in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria.
tldr: Averages the values in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to average, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are averaged.

basicExample.description: Average the Yield of apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 (Tree=Apple, Height>10) matches two rows with Yield 14 and 10; the mean is (14+10)/2 = 12.

advancedExamples.title: Average a different column
advancedExamples.scenario: Average Profit for the same matching trees
advancedExamples.description: Change only the field to Profit (column 5).
advancedExamples.explanation: The two matching rows have Profit 105 and 75, so the average is (105+75)/2 = 90.

advancedExamples.title: Single matching record
advancedExamples.description: With criteria Tree=Cherry, only one record matches, so the average equals that value.
advancedExamples.explanation: Only the cherry row (Yield 9) matches, so the mean is 9.

howItWorks: DAVERAGE filters the database to rows matching the criteria, sums the numeric values in the specified field, and divides by the count of those numeric values. Text and blank cells in the field are excluded from both the sum and the count.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Only numeric values in the field are considered; text and blanks are ignored.
If no records match, DAVERAGE returns the #DIV/0! error.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: No records matched the criteria, so the count of numeric values was zero.
commonErrors.fix: Check the criteria so at least one record matches, or verify header spelling.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DAVERAGE works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: Does DAVERAGE include blank cells in the count?
faq.answer: No. Only numeric values in the matching rows are counted and averaged.

faq.question: What happens with a single matching record?
faq.answer: The average equals that one value.

faq.question: How is DAVERAGE different from AVERAGEIF?
faq.answer: DAVERAGE filters a multi-column database by a full criteria range, while AVERAGEIF applies a single condition to one range.
